events.authority.the_file_catches_up.bod: It is not a checkpoint, exactly. A car, two people, and a question about where you crossed and when. One of them already has the answer written down and is checking it against your face. The other is watching your hands.
events.authority.the_file_catches_up.out: You tell it straight, twice, the same way both times. Whatever they were checking, it matches. They thank you, which is somehow worse than not being thanked.
Nothing you say is wrong. It simply takes an hour to establish that, and by the end there is a second sheet of paper with your name at the top of it.
They decide it is easier to sort out in the morning. There is a bench, a light nobody turns off, and a great deal of time to think about which answer did it.
You stop answering and start waiting. It takes four minutes for the whole thing to become more trouble than it is worth to them. They wave you off mid-sentence.
They have more patience than you do, and considerably more paperwork. The conversation ends where these conversations end.
The question is understood immediately, which tells you something about the week they have been having. The sheet of paper does not come back out.
You misjudge the room by a considerable margin. Now there is the original problem, and there is what you just said, and the second one is worse.
